description: F1-S6 dry-run metrics baseline. The 27 Jul 2026 observed sample (issue #9 comments 2026-07-27T21:43:41Z and 2026-07-27T21:47:31Z) transcribed as execution=conventional FactoryPrRecord entries per D136 (data delivered separately from logic), D143 (Wilson-lower-bound confidence, at least 3 distinct issue types, enforced audit sampling) and the ratified 9b contract (D147). These are illustrative baseline EVIDENCE, not factory PRs: evaluatePromotion filters to execution=factory only, so nothing here counts toward any ratchet promotion, diversity, or audit-owed decision, and the audit ledger is empty by design. Field values follow the runbook capture procedure (docs/factory-runbook.md, Metrics baseline capture (9b)). Caveats carried from the source sample, recorded so no value here is mistaken for instrumented precision: (1) n=1 session, no controlled comparison, poor issue-type diversity (one hardening slice #150, one security fix #153 for issue #151, one docs/state reconciliation #152). (2) humanTouchMinutes was NOT instrumented and the operator declined to estimate it (not reported rather than estimated). The merged schema (Unit 1) types this field as a required non-nullable number with no way to encode unavailable, so it is recorded as 0 strictly as an UN-INSTRUMENTED SENTINEL, never a measured zero. It is inert: no summariser sums it and it gates nothing in evaluatePromotion. Making the field nullable so un-instrumented effort is representable honestly is a Unit-1 schema question routed as a follow-on, deliberately out of this data-only slice. (3) lensCosts records the REVIEW-ALLOCATION cost the field exists to study (contract 1.3 and the 21:47 operator comment): the sub-agent review lenses and the cloud review lenses. The always-on automated CI gates (ci, codeql, dependency-review, codecov, mutation-gate) are not enumerated per-PR because their cost is fixed CI infrastructure, not the review-allocation variable. Within that scope, per-lens token cost is concrete ONLY for PR #150, whose split the operator documented (factory-security-reviewer 155k, schema-migration-reviewer 111k, qa 109k, pr-triage 107k of a roughly 482k sub-agent total); every other review lens that ran but whose per-PR cost was not separately measured is recorded with tokens=null (measured-unavailable, never coerced to 0, surfaced as unknownCostEntries) rather than omitted, including the cloud review lenses on #150 and the claude-code-review control run plus the codex-connector clean verdict on #152. wallClockSeconds is null throughout: only 8 to 23 minute per-invocation ranges were recorded, not per-lens figures. Scope: this manifest transcribes the operator's 27 Jul sample as the authoritative source and does NOT forensically reconstruct additional lens executions or wall-clock durations from 10-day-old Actions job metadata that the sample did not capture; a review lens the sample did not record (for example spec-grounded-review) is therefore absent rather than asserted with an inferred cost, because inventing a not-in-source execution would itself inject unvalidated evidence. (4) Post-ready rework rounds were 0 across the session. postOpenReviewRounds follows the runbook definition (review/fix rounds after the PR OPENED, not only after ready): #150 was opened as a draft (D103 shift-left), its first draft push failed CI on the mutation gate (firstPassCiGreen=false) and was corrected by one further push before ready, so it records postOpenReviewRounds=1, a draft-phase CI fix folded before any review lens ran, NOT post-ready churn. #152 and #153 were first-pass green (firstPassCiGreen=true). #152 records postOpenReviewRounds=1: its pr-triage catch was a completed post-open review round (it prompted the dated authorization comment before merge) even though #152's own diff needed no fix push. #153 had no post-open review/fix round (postOpenReviewRounds=0; its fsr findings all landed pre-push). The mutation-gate failure on #150 is recorded both as firstPassCiGreen=false and as a mutation-gate reviewFinding (runbook: every substantive check result is a finding), marked downstream-gate-would-catch so no review lens earns credit for it. (5) pr-triage recorded 0 overrides across the session (triageOverridden=false everywhere). (6) securitySurface records routing-set membership per the capture procedure (apply the factory-security-reviewer routing set to the PR path list), NOT whether an fsr pass happened to run: true for #150 (workflow plus grant-boundary Python), #152 (docs/state/registry.md is in the routing set, though the session handled it as a docs sync and ran no fsr pass), and #153 (workflow plus tests/factory). A conventional record's audit obligation is inert here because the ratchet consumes factory records only and the ledger is empty by design. (7) Counterfactual markers use the source's only explicit assessments: the committed mutation-baseline claim was caught by the CI mutation gate regardless of any review lens (downstream-gate-would-catch), the factory-security-reviewer guard-bypass blockers were unique to that adversarial lens (unique-to-lens), and every other finding is unassessed and therefore never credited. (8) Findings from the pre-open sub-agent lenses (factory-security-reviewer, schema-migration-reviewer, codex-local-review, pr-triage) landed pre-push, so no GitHub PR review thread exists to link; the claude-code-review style nit and the Codex clean verdicts on #150 were post-ready. Each description cites the retained aggregate source (the issue #9 sample of 2026-07-27T21:43:41Z, which records per-lens counts, not individual findings) and notes that individual detail was not separately retained. The two substantive pr-triage catches the sample reports are preserved as pr-triage findings: one is attributed to #152 (evidenced by the 2026-07-27T21:29:02Z authorization-recording comment), the other is unattributed in the source and recorded on the #150 record; the attribution state is flagged in each description. sampledForAudit is false throughout: the R-percent draw applies to factory records, and no draw was performed for these conventional baseline entries.
